questions.q: Small text files a website stores in your browser to remember sessions and preferences are called:
questions.solution: Cookies hold site-specific data (login sessions, carts, preferences, tracking IDs). They are plain text files - not programs and not viruses.
questions.shortcut: Website's memory of you = cookie.

questions.q: A cell displaying ######## (hash marks) indicates:
options: The column is too narrow to show the value
questions.solution: Excel fills the cell with # symbols when the formatted number cannot fit the column width - widen the column. It is a display condition, not an error.
questions.shortcut: Hashes = width, never an error code.

questions.q: Which utility shows running processes, CPU/RAM usage and startup programs in Windows?
questions.solution: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) displays processes, performance graphs, startup impact and lets you end tasks. Device Manager lists hardware/drivers; Disk Management handles partitions; Event Viewer logs system events.
questions.shortcut: Running apps + performance = Task Manager; hardware + drivers = Device Manager.

questions.q: A network confined to a single office building is classified as a:
questions.solution: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a room, building or campus. MANs span cities, WANs span countries/continents.
questions.shortcut: Local = LAN; City = MAN; Wide/world = WAN.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** India's cities are growing at a breathtaking pace. **P:** This puts heavy pressure on housing and transport. **Q:** New settlements are spilling beyond city limits. **R:** The government has launched new urban schemes in reply. **S:** Slums are spreading along every highway. **6.** Whether they succeed, only time will tell.
questions.solution: **P** follows S1 (growth → pressure, 'This' = growth) → **Q** details the spill-over → **S** shows the slum result on the ground → **R** brings the reply (schemes) just before S6's verdict. PQSR.
questions.shortcut: Demonstrative pair S1→P; ground-level detail before the response; R is the closing action.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who talks in his sleep
questions.solution: Somni = sleep + loqui = speak → **somniloquist**. *Somnambulist* walks in sleep (ambul = walk) — the classic sibling trap; *insomniac* cannot sleep at all.
questions.shortcut: somni- (sleep) + verb root decides: walk vs speak.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said, "I have finished my work."
options: She said that she has finished her work.
She said that she finished her work.
She said that she had finish her work.
She said that she had finished her work.
questions.solution: Present perfect → **past perfect**: had finished; I → she; my → her. B skips the backshift; C drops to simple past; D breaks the participle.
questions.shortcut: have finished → had finished.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Hardly had the guests arrived ___ it started raining.
questions.solution: *Hardly* is paired with **when** (or *before*). *than* belongs with *no sooner*; *then* and *that* are not correlative partners here.
questions.shortcut: Hardly/Scarcely → when; No sooner → than.

questions.q: **Kathakali**, the dance-drama known for its elaborate green face make-up, is a classical dance of —
questions.solution: **Kathakali** is from **Kerala**; the poet Vallathol founded Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) to revive it. Karnataka's comparable dance-drama is Yakshagana (a folk form).
questions.shortcut: **K**athakali = **K**erala.

questions.q: DRDO test-fired the Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM) in June 2026 from —
options: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha
questions.solution: The LRLACM was flight-tested on 15 June 2026 from **Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Island (Wheeler Island), off the Odisha coast** — DRDO's dedicated missile-test island.
questions.shortcut: Missile tests → Abdul Kalam Island; space launches → Sriharikota.

questions.q: **National Science Day** is celebrated in India on —
questions.solution: **28 February** marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the **Raman effect** in 1928. 7 November is Raman's birthday; 11 May is National Technology Day (Pokhran-II, 1998); 15 September is Engineers' Day.
questions.shortcut: Science Day = discovery date, not birthday.

questions.q: The **tripartite struggle** among the Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas was fought for control over —
questions.solution: From the 8th to the 10th century the three powers fought for **Kannauj**, the symbol of supremacy over north India after Harsha.
questions.shortcut: PPR fight for **K**annauj.

questions.q: A number when divided by 893 leaves a remainder of 193. What will be the remainder when the same number is divided by 47?
questions.solution:
Let $N = 893k + 193$. Since $893 = 47 \times 19$, $893k$ is a multiple of 47.
So the remainder is $193 \bmod 47$: $193 = 4 \times 47 + 5$ ⇒ **5**.
questions.shortcut: 47 divides 893, so just divide the old remainder: 193 − 188 = 5.

questions.q: A completes a job in 10 days and B in 20 days. Working together, they complete it in:
questions.solution: $\frac{ab}{a+b} = \frac{10 \times 20}{30} = \frac{20}{3} = 6\frac{2}{3}$ days.
questions.shortcut: LCM: 20 units, 3/day ⇒ 6⅔ days.

questions.q: If $a+b+c=12$ and $a^2+b^2+c^2=50$, then what is the value of $a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc$?
questions.shortcut: $12\times(50-47)=36$. Trap 1164 adds 47 instead of subtracting.
questions.pattern: $a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc$ from sum and sum of squares

questions.q: If $\tan\theta=\dfrac{3}{4}$, the value of $\dfrac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta-\cos\theta}$ is:
questions.solution:
Divide numerator and denominator by $\cos\theta$:

$\dfrac{\tan\theta+1}{\tan\theta-1}=\dfrac{\frac34+1}{\frac34-1}=\dfrac{7/4}{-1/4}=-7$.
questions.shortcut: Divide through by $\cos\theta$: $(t+1)/(t-1)$ with $t=\frac34$ → $-7$. (Same trick works for any sin/cos ratio expression.)
questions.pattern: divide by cos to use tan

questions.q:
**Statements:** No glass is metal. Some metals are solids.

**Conclusions:** I. Some solids are not glass. II. All glasses are solids.
questions.solution: The solid that is metal cannot be glass (glass and metal never meet) → some solids are not glass: I follows. Glass has no forced link with solids → II fails. **Only I.**
questions.shortcut: A 'Some metal are solid' element inherits metal's full exile from glass.

questions.q: Select the related letters: **CAT : XZG :: SUN : ?**
questions.shortcut: Position sum 27 = Atbash; convert through the opposite-pairs table in one pass.

Final: **4 holes**.
questions.shortcut: Mirror across the horizontal midline.

questions.q: **X is older than Y. Z is younger than W. V is older than X. W is older than V. Y is older than Z.** Who is the **third oldest**?
questions.solution: Chain: W > V > X > Y > Z (W is pinned above V; V above X; X above Y; Y above Z; and Z < W is automatic). Third oldest = **X**.
questions.shortcut: Build the spine W > V > X, then hang Y and Z below X.
